qt: to the Commission Kostas Papadakis (NI) Subject:

The large-scale, coordinated mobilisation of struggling farmers, both in Greece and throughout the EU, is directly opposing the effects of the CAP, whose measures are exacerbating the blatant exploitation of farmers for the benefit of agri-food groups. In full alignment with similar practices seen in other EU Member States, the bourgeois state in Greece is responding to farmers’ reasonable demands prompted by their need to survive, by turning to authoritarianism, terrorism and the systematic criminalisation of the struggles. It is telling that there are currently more than 1 000 ongoing cases against struggling farmers for the 2025-2026 protests, with a plethora of prosecutions, summonses and referrals to trials. Meanwhile, the Nea Dimokratia Government is obstinately refusing to legislate to put an end to the prosecutions and close the case files. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What is its take on the fact that all the EU’s famous ‘European rule of law’ does is endorse harsh treatment, terror, hundreds of prosecutions and the criminalisation of the fight of farmers struggling for their livelihoods, both in Greece and in other Member States?

Where does it stand on the provocative regime of impunity and concealment enjoyed by Nea Dimokratia government officials and ministers in the context of the OPEKEPE scandal, for which the EU bears great responsibility, while farmers have to endure brutal state repression for seeking to claim back the subsidies owed to them?
